meta_title: Rounded Corners Image Tool | Free Image Corner Rounder
meta_description: Add rounded corners to photos instantly. The easiest image corner rounder tool online. Export as PNG with transparent corners securely.
subtitle: Create smooth, perfectly rounded corners for your images. Ideal for app icons, profile pictures, and web graphics.

tool_workspace.description: Upload an image and adjust the radius slider to create perfect rounded corners.

requirements.intro: The slider sets the corner radius as a percentage of half the image’s shorter side, so the same setting looks the same on small and large images.

rows.value: Subtly rounded corners, like app screenshots and cards. 25% is the starting value.
Strongly rounded corners, similar to app icons.

rows.label: 100% on a square image
rows.value: A perfect circle, ideal for profile pictures and avatars.

rows.label: 100% on a rectangle
rows.value: A pill shape with fully rounded ends.

rows.label: Output
rows.value: Always PNG, so the cut-away corners are transparent rather than white or black.

notes: For a circular profile picture, crop the photo to a square first with the image cropper, then set the radius to 100%.
The output is PNG to keep the corners transparent. If you need a smaller file, convert it to WebP, which also keeps transparency.
If you convert the result to JPG, the transparent corners turn white.

how_to.title: How to round the corners of an image
how_to.step1_text: Select or drag in one or more JPG, PNG or WebP files. Nothing is uploaded.
how_to.step2_text: Move the slider to choose how rounded the corners are. 100% gives a circle on square images.
how_to.step3_text: Click the apply button to download a PNG with transparent corners, or a ZIP for several images.

items.q: How do I make a circular profile picture?
items.a: Crop the image to a square (1:1) first, then set the radius to 100%. The result is a circle with a transparent background.

items.q: Why is the output a PNG?
items.a: JPG cannot store transparency, so the rounded corners would be filled with a solid colour. PNG keeps them transparent.

items.q: Why is my PNG larger than the original JPG?
items.a: PNG is lossless. For a smaller file that keeps the transparent corners, convert the PNG to WebP.
